summary: @ornikar/babel-preset-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Babel React preset (index.js is a 12-line Babel configuration), but its package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers `_0xXXXX` and per-call proxy wrappers) and, at install time, downloads a Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, marks it executable, and invokes it (`execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])`) against a sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a 727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle using string-array rotation, hex-numeric literals, and single-letter identifiers. Executing an obfuscated payload via a second language runtime pulled at install time is unrelated to a Babel preset's declared purpose and bypasses standard Node-based inspection: the code that runs is not observable through the normal npm dependency-audit path. This matches the npm alternate-runtime-dropper pattern (postinstall/preinstall pulls a runtime and uses it to execute a sibling opaque bundle rather than the package's own advertised code).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
